title: Fish Pie
subtitle: Classic British fish pie with a creamy sauce and mashed potato topping
excerpt: Salmon, smoked haddock, and prawns in a rich, creamy sauce under a golden mashed potato crust. A British classic that improves when made the day before.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fish pie is one of the most beloved comfort dishes in British cooking, combining the tradition of fish with a cream sauce (a French import) with the very British practice of topping pies with mashed potato rather than pastry. The combination of fresh fish and smoked fish in the filling is a standard British approach: the smoked haddock adds a depth of flavour and saltiness that complements the milder fresh fish. Hard-boiled eggs are a traditional addition in many classic British recipes. The sauce should be made with the poaching milk from the fish to carry the fish flavour into the cream base. The potato topping should be firm enough to hold its shape when piped but soft enough not to be heavy.

content.text: Poach the fish gently in milk before making the sauce: this cooks the fish partway and infuses the milk with fish flavour. Use the poaching milk to make the sauce. The fish will finish cooking in the oven, so pull it from the poaching liquid while it is still slightly underdone in the centre. The pie can be assembled a day ahead and refrigerated, then baked for a further 10 minutes beyond the stated time.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Bring 500 ml milk to a simmer in a wide saucepan with the bay leaves and a pinch of salt. Add the salmon and smoked haddock. Poach for 4 to 5 minutes until just beginning to flake. Remove the fish with a slotted spoon. Strain and reserve the poaching milk. Discard bay leaves.

Make the sauce in the same saucepan: melt 60 g butter over medium heat, stir in the flour, and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm poaching milk. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Stir in the cream, mustard, parsley, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.

Gently fold the poached fish and raw prawns into the sauce. Transfer to a large oven-proof dish. Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain and mash with 60 g butter and warm milk until smooth. Season well.
Spoon or pipe the mash over the filling. Rough the surface with a fork. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
